CLIMATE ACTION 
Climate Action Plan (CAP) 
1. Northwest Regional Assembly (NWRA) Decarbonising Zone Scheme (ERDF funding) letter of offer for 
€240,401 for Carrick Flood Defence and €49,070 for a Tree & Hedgerow Management Plan (11 June 
2026). Project-related work to be completed by Q2 2027. 
2. LASNTG / CARO webinar series for 2026 (build capacity for whole of Council team) continued with 
Pathfinder (4 June 2026), Renewable Gas in Transport (19 June 2026) 
3. Climate Action assisting Community Development in rollout of the Local Environment Action Fund for 
Tidy Towns and Community Groups (call open 15 June 2026) 
4. Local Authority Waters Programme (LAWPRO) Nature-based Solutions for Local Authorities grant 
agreement (15 June 2026) for €75,000 for Bio-Retention Swale(s) in the Dromod to Rooskey Greyway. 
Works to be completed by 6 November 2026. 
5. Decarbonising Zone Demonstrator Fund confirmed (16 June 2026), with €56,000 available for actions 
that align with actions in the Leitrim Climate Action Plan with works to be completed for reclaim in 
November 2026.  Department produced parameter document, webinar (22 June 2026) and FAQs. 
6. IKC3 training programme to build capacity in groups in around the Decarbonising Zone concluded 
with a summit for participants across all of the 5 no counties (Galway City, Leitrim, Offaly, 
Roscommon, Westmeath) in Trinity College (30 June 2026) 
7. District Heating feasibility report completed for Carrick-on-Shannon.  Preferred option of water 
source heat pump from River Shannon, with Energy Centre adjacent to the Áras complex with 
associated district heating network emanating from there. 
8. Local Authority Climate Action Plan Guidelines for the making of the next LACAPs are under review 
kicking off with a series of CARO workshops of CA staff in June 2026 
 
Community Climate Action Programme (CCAP) Fund  
1. Final drawdown made for completed projects under CCAP Phase 1 for Strand 1 and Strand 1a made 
end of June 2026 
2. Letters of Offer made for projects announced for funding by the Department for CCAP, Phase 2, Strand 
1 (4 June 2026) 
 
Biodiversity 
1. Biodiversity Newsletter for interested groups began circulation (17 June 2026) 
2. Appointment of consultant for Provision of ecological services for Ancient Oak Woodland at Garadice 
Lough (25 June 2026) 
3. Tidy Towns LEADER funding for a feasibility study on a Wetland Eco Park as outlined in 
recommendation in the Town Centre First Report, public consultation event in the Market Yard on 25 
June 2026, McCloy Consultants present on the day. 
 
COMMUNITY AND INTERGATION 
Age Friendly Programme   
Delivered Age Friendly Business training to nine business representatives in The Hive. Work progressing 
with the representatives to have their businesses officially certified by Age Friendly Ireland. 
Healthy Ireland

6 
 
90% of Healthy Ireland grant funding has been distributed. The new Healthy County Coordinator 
commenced on 22nd of June and is engaging with partners to monitor programme delivery. 
Pobal has confirmed the extension of the Healthy Ireland Framework to the end of 2027, with updated 
2027 workplan templates due to issue in the coming weeks. Following discussions with Pobal, the 
current breastfeeding outcome is under review, with consideration being given to a new priority area for 
2027. Any proposed outcome changes will be brought to the LCDC for approval. 
 
The Fit Farmers App is now live in Leitrim. A launch event is being planned for 27 August in Mohill Library, 
aligned with mart day activities, to promote the app and recruit participants for a six-week Fit Farmers 
programme taking place in November 2026 in Drunshambo. 
 
Two of four Music & Memory Cafés have launched, including the Mohill Library launch on 3rd of July, 
delivered with Understanding Together Dementia. 
 
Community Recognition Fund 
As at the end of June 2026, 9 of these projects have been completed with funding fully drawn down from 
the Department of Rural and Community Development and an Gaeltacht. 
 
Playgrounds 
Leitrim County Council secured funding of €22,000 from the Department of Children, Disability and 
Equality an inclusive and accessible upgrade of Dristernan Playground, Drumshanbo. Contractor has 
been appointed. 
 
Leitrim PEACEPLUS Action Plan (1.1) 
 
Thriving & Peaceful Communities  
• QQI Level 7 – closing residential took place in Maynooth University on the 19th/20th June. Final 
projects presented and planning for graduation underway.  
• Virtual Reality Program Equipment – This will be delivered in a number of locations throughout 
the county. First VR programme taking place 17th July in the Irish Wheelchair Association in 
Carrick on Shannon. 
 
PEACEPLUS Shannonside Peace Arena (1.4) 
• 
The SRC construction tender remains active within the tender response period.  Six clarification 
queries have been received from prospective contractors, with site visits scheduled to continue 
throughout July. 
• 
The second draft of the LSSIF Preliminary Business Case was submitted in mid-June; further 
queries and clarifications are currently awaited. 
• 
Engagement with the SRC Communications Team took place in early June, with preparations 
underway for the publication of the second newsletter in August. 
• 
A review of SRC BREEAM requirements has been completed; the project is currently rated at 
“Good” and progress is being made towards achieving a “Very Good” rating in advance of 
construction commencement. 
•

• Crowleys DFK auditors have been working on certifying our claims. Under the Council Action Plan 
we have 10 Claims up on the Jems Portal from Oct 2023 to March 202. Claim periods are

• Under the Shannonside Peace Arena there are 6 Claims on the portal from November 2024 to 
April 2025.  LCC have zero expenditure for first 2 claim periods. We have responded to detailed 
queries on Claim 6 and are awaiting certification on these.  
 
Local Community Safety Partnership 
A public consultation has now been completed and consultation findings are being analysed to inform 
the development of the Local Community Safety Plan. The Community Safety Plan Subcommittee has 
been established and will support the identification of priorities and development of actions for 
inclusion in the Plan. 
Two applications were submitted under the Community Safety Fund by Leitrim LCSP. 
Leitrim Local Community Development Committee 
At its meeting on 17th June 2026, the Leitrim Local Community Development Committee (LCDC) 
approved two LEADER projects with a total funding value of €44,736.75.  
Local Authority Integration Team (LAIT) 
The Integration Team delivered a total of thirteen clinics supporting individuals and families to access 
appropriate services. 
• 
Six clinics were held for Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTP). 
• 
Seven clinics were delivered across IPAS Centres. 
In collaboration with Revenue Services, the Integration Team delivered an Introduction to PAYE Services 
information session. The sessions were hosted in Dromahair and Ballinamore, providing attendees with 
practical information on PAYE services and supports. 
Confidence in the Kitchen – Children’s Cookery Classes programme concluded in Dromahair during 
June. This four-week initiative, delivered in partnership with Sligo Family Resource Centre, aimed to 
enhance children’s confidence and develop their practical cookery skills in a fun and supportive 
environment. A total of 15 children attended, comprising a mix of children from the IPAS Centre and the 
local community. 
 
The Wellbeing Advantage Workshop Series, delivered in partnership with Healthy Ireland, continued 
throughout June. This 12-week programme promotes health and wellbeing through a range of activities, 
including walking and running groups, wellbeing information sessions, and individual health 
assessments. 
 
Refugee Week, a national celebration held from 15–21 June, was centred on the theme “Courage.” The 
Integration Team worked collaboratively with a range of local organisations to deliver three events 
across County Leitrim. 
 
On 17 June, in partnership with Scoil Chlann Naofa, Ballinamore, a screening of The Breadwinner was 
hosted at the Island Theatre, with attendance from pupils in 4th to 6th class. Also on the same day, the

8 
 
Integration Team collaborated with the Leitrim International Community Group to facilitate a Basket 
Weaving Workshop in Ballinamore Library, encouraging community participation. 
On 18 June, the Integration Team partnered with Leitrim Development Company to deliver a Hoody 
Design Workshop in Dromahair. Participants expressed the Refugee Week theme of “Courage” through 
their individual designs. 
 
Irish Refugee Protection Programme – To date, the Department has completed inspections of two 
properties, and two families have been successfully resettled. These households comprise a total of 5 
adults and 7 children. 
Work is also underway to prepare and furnish two additional properties. We are currently awaiting 
confirmation from the Department of inspection dates for both properties.

Over the month of June all libraries were busy with the usual events such as class visits, reading groups 
and writer group meetings, English and Irish language classes, art & craft sessions, games 
afternoons/evenings, and bridge club. 
In addition, Ballinamore Library hosted a training evening for volunteers participating in the Leitrim 
Community Holy Well Project with the Heritage Office and Archaeology Plan, as well as a Stay & Play 
session for the regular Breastfeeding Group with Lifestart, and Carrick-on-Shannon Library hosted an 
interactive Age-Friendly AI information session. 
Cruinniú na nÓg 
Almost 330 participants engaged in a wide range of free creative events and activities across the library 
branch network to mark Cruinniú na nÓg.  Manorhamilton and Kiltyclogher Libraries facilitated mock 
archaeological digs, followed by axe-making workshops.  Mohill and Carrigallen Libraries both partnered 
with Music Generation to provide opportunities for children to engage creatively with music.  
Drumshanbo Library hosted birdhouse and mug-making workshops, while Dromahair Library ran both 
storytelling and laser-cutting sessions.    
Summer Stars 
The Summer Stars national reading campaign encourages children to continue reading during the 
summer holidays.  Launching on June 2nd, a county-wide calendar of events taking place over July and 
August was sent to all National Schools in the county and is being promoted extensively in branches and 
online.  All participants registered in the programme receive free Summer Stars merchandise each time 
they return a completed reading card to their local library, are in with a chance to win vouchers and a 
grand surprise prize at the close of the summer! 
Poetry Festival Launch 
Carrick-on-Shannon Library hosted the launch of the inaugural Between the Lines Poetry Festival on 
Thursday 4th June.  The evening consisted of readings from poet Gerry Boland, Councillor Enda Stenson, 
Kathleen Coleman and Senior Executive Librarian Catherine Lee.  The festival took place on Saturday 27th 
June in St. George’s Heritage & Visitor Centre.  
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, REGENERATION, SUSTAINABLE 
TRANSPORT & EMERGENCY SERVICES 
 
 
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT 
Leitrim’s Diaspora Strategy 2026-2030 
The Diaspora Strategy was presented to the Enterprise and Economic Development Strategic Policy 
Committee on 12th June; planning is progressing for the official launch event. 
 
Leitrim Economic Forum

10 
 
Work continues the Development of the Economic and Skills strategy for Leitrim and on the planning of 
the Leitrim Ambassadors Summit, two initiatives of the Forum.  The summit is scheduled for September 
2026. 
 
Shaping Leitrim- A Place led Economic and Skills Strategy for Leitrim 2026-2035. 
A draft document his currently under review. Two workshops were held in June to validate the finding 
with stakeholders. One -to -one meetings are taking place with action owners to progress sign off on 
action plan.  
 
Global Business Network 
The next meeting of the group is scheduled for 30th September 2026. 
 
"Most Definitely Leitrim" Remote Working/Croí Cónaithe Social Media Campaign 
The campaign launched on Wed 17th June and was picked up by national media. Interviews took place 
on RTE Morning Ireland, Shannon side FM, and RTE2FM. The campaign has started well and will continue 
for 3 months. 
 
DRCDG Funded Schemes 
The Outdoor Recreation Investment Scheme opened during June and was widely promoted in print and 
online. A webinar has been scheduled for early July.  
 
TOURISM 
Marketing Campaign 
The Destination Leitrim marketing campaign continued throughout June, featuring radio 
advertisements on Cool Radio Northern Ireland, targeted digital marketing activity, and a high 
engagement prize giveaway on 2FM delivered in partnership with Maguires Red Door Cottages and The 
Shed Distillery. 
 
Alongside this, a dedicated daycation regional campaign was rolled out to promote the short-break 
market. The campaign showcased a wide variety of attractions across County Leitrim and encouraged 
audiences to plan their visit through a clear call-to-action directing them to the enjoy Leitrim website. 
 
Le Boat Conference 
Le Boat hosted its annual conference in County Leitrim at the beginning of the month, welcoming 
delegates from across Europe and Canada. 
 
During their stay, delegates explored a wide range of local attractions and experiences. Despite mixed 
weather conditions, the group thoroughly enjoyed their time in Leitrim and left with a strong 
appreciation for the county’s distinctive character and hospitality. Their first-hand experience of 
Leitrim’s landscapes, culture, and cruising offering positions them well to promote the destination to 
their customers. 
 
The Tourism team also had the opportunity to meet with the senior Le Boat team to present on the 
cruising product in Leitrim. The discussion focused on how we can deepen collaboration to further 
promote the cruising experience to overseas markets, strengthening Leitrim’s profile as a standout 
holiday destination. 
 
Publicity

11 
 
National and regional PR coverage was secured for the new Water Park at Lough Allen Adventure in 
Drumshanbo, Co. Leitrim, positioning it as an exciting, family-friendly attraction. The coverage also 
highlighted the many nearby visitors’ experiences, reinforcing Leitrim’s growing strength as a family-
focused destination. 
 
The water park opened in May and will open through September (daily throughout July and August), it is 
an ideal choice for school tours, sports club’s birthday parties, corporate groups and family days out. 
 
National Outdoor Recreation Conference 
The Tourism Team attended the National Outdoor Recreation Conference held at the Slieve Russell 
Hotel. The event was addressed by Minister Peter Burke from the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and 
Employment and featured a wide range of speakers from across the outdoor recreation sector. 
 
The conference provided valuable insights into national policy developments, emerging trends, and best 
practice approaches in recreation planning and management. It also offered opportunities to engage 
with industry leaders and partner organisations, supporting ongoing collaboration to strengthen 
outdoor recreation experiences in County Leitrim. 
 
TOWN REGENERATION 
Croí Conaithe – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grants 
13 new applications were received in June 2026, total number of applications in 2026 is 75 during this 
reporting period, 34 grant payments were processed 2026. 
 
Local Development SPC 
The Local Development SPC was held on the 2nd June 2026 was held offsite in Carrigallan with presentation 
from Mervin & Clifford Richardson of Jetwash International Ltd regarding their successful planning 
application for a renewable energy solar farm in Carrigallen. 
 
ROADS 
N4 Carrick-on-Shannon Bypass & Traffic Management Project 
The N4 Carrick-on-Shannon Bypass & Traffic Management Project is progressing as follows: 
• 
Phase 3 – Design and Environmental Evaluation is ongoing. 
• 
The Phase 3 Environmental Impact Assessment Report (EIAR) is currently being updated based on comments 
from TII & Legal review 
• 
Ground investigation fieldwork has been completed on-site in the Material Deposition/Reuse Area located 
east of the River Shannon. 
• 
The River Shannon Bridge is under final design with input from specialist bridge architects 
• 
The Preliminary Business Case and associated Cost Benefit Analysis is currently under final update 
• 
The Draft CPO/PRO deposit maps and schedule have been prepared and are under review 
• 
All phase 3 surveys such as Ground Investigation, Topographical, archaeological, ecological etc. are now 
complete on site

Road Safety 
The Road Safety Office of Leitrim County Council in partnership with the RSA and the Cowboy & Heroes Festival 
organizer’s, arranged for the provision of the Flinebox mobile self-service breathalyser at the Cowboys & Heroes 
Festival in Drumcoura over the June Bank Holiday Weekend.  The Flinebox is a mobile self-service breathalyser 
which the RSA can make available for various festivals and events. The Flinebox self-service breathalyser gives 
festival goers the option to check their alcohol level before travelling, helping them to make informed, responsible 
choices and avoid taking risks on the roads. 
 
ACTIVE TRAVEL 
Part 8 Planning approved for the following at June MD’s and now at Detailed Design Stage: 
• 
Drumshanbo – Town Junction upgrade  
• 
Carrick on Shannon – Attifinlay Roundabout to Summerhill Active Travel Scheme   
 
Safe Route to Schools 
• 
St. Clare’s NS, Manorhamilton – Construction to commence in Q3/2026. 
 
• 
Drumshanbo Vocational School – Construction to commence in July by Contractor. 
 
 
CAPITAL PROJECTS 
Carrick on Shannon Flood Relief Scheme  
The Legal Review of the first draft Environmental Impact Assessment Report (EIAR) has now been 
completed. A Buildability Workshop is scheduled for 15 July to finalise the Scheme Design in preparation 
for the planning submission. 
 
The PR3 and AG1 approvals are currently with OPW Senior Management for review and consideration. 
Leitrim County Council (LCC) is awaiting approval of these documents before we proceed with the 
submission of the scheme to An Coimisiún Pleanála. Subject to the necessary approvals being received, 
the planning submission remains programmed for Q4 2026. 
 
Leitrim Village Flood Relief Scheme  
Substantial progress has been made on the approach to Compiling a Business case for the Scheme.  Full 
details of the project are available on website www.leitrimvillagefrs.ie. 
The first draft of the Environmental Impact Assessment Report (EIAR) is nearing completion. 
Submission of a Business Case and Preparing PR3 and AG1 approvals are scheduled in Q3 2026.  
   
Mohill Flood Relief Scheme  
The hydraulic analysis and economic feasibility on this project to determine the need/extent for flood 
defenses have been substantially complete in Mohill by OPW in partnership with LCC Capital Projects 
Office. We await OPW’s determination, following  a business case submitted to them in September 2024. 
OPW have mentioned that may fall under the Minor Works Scheme, before Scheme progressing to 
Planning Consent & Construction. 
 
OPW Minor Flood Schemes 
Dromahair Scheme  
The project was tendered in March 2026, with tender assessments completed in April 2026. Following 
evaluation of the submissions received, approval was sought from and subsequently granted by the 
Office of Public Works (OPW), as the most economically advantageous tender exceeded the funding 
allocation available for the project.

13 
 
Source Civil has since received its Letter of Acceptance, with the contractor's construction programme 
indicating a planned commencement of works in August 2026. The project is therefore progressing 
towards the construction phase. 
 
Leitrim Village (Keadue Road Scheme) Scheme  
The Minor works scheme is substantially complete. 
 
Manorhamilton Minor Works Scheme  
This Minor works scheme is substantially complete.  
 
Carrick on Shannon Urban Regeneration Scheme 
A Substantial completion has been issued for the Lighting Contact for the Linear Park Marina and the 
pedestrian bridge on the N4, Defects to be completed be the contractor.  
 
Manorhamilton Public Realm Scheme 
Contract No 1 for public realm works on Main Street has been completed. Works on Contract No 2 for the 
realignment of the access road to Enterprise lands off Park Road is underway on site and is expected to 
be completed by year end. 
 
Mohill Public Realm Scheme  
Works have been completed. A Substantial Completion Certificate has been issued to the Contractor.  
 
Drumshanbo ExChange.  
Crosserlough Construction have commenced work on Site with completion of the project expected in Q4 
2027. 
 
Drumshanbo Food Innovation & Knowledge Hub   
A planning application for Phase 2 of this development is currently on public display, when consent is 
granted detailed design for the scheme will commence. 
Shannonside Recreational Campus 
The construction tender was published with closing date for receipt of tenders 11th August 2026. Works 
are expected to commence on site in early to mid-October 2026. 
Carrick Arts and Community Centre (Coleman's Building, Main Street) 
Works are now substantially complete and we are awaiting the ESB connection. Following connection, 
the M&E systems will require testing and commissioning, with final snagging works to be completed 
prior to handover. Handover are expected in late July 2026. 
Manorhamilton NCYS Building 
Works have been completed. The final account has been agreed and the project closed out. 
Leitrim Village Community Facility  
Further information requested in relation to the planning application has now been submitted to the 
Planning Authority by Davitt Plan and Design & Associates and a decision is pending.   
 
SLNCR Greenway – Sligo to Enniskillen  
Phase 2 deliverables and reports are now uploaded to the SLNCR dedicated web site. Full details on web 
site SLNCR and key milestones achieved with infographic of information. Phase 3 Design & 
Environmental Phase is ongoing.  The PLO’s are meeting Landowner/Property owners on an ongoing

14 
 
basis discussing the Emerging Preferred Route (EPR). LiDAR/Drone Surveys (ROI) are completed. 
Topographical & Hydrographical Surveys (ROI only) currently ongoing in Co. Sligo. Traffic surveys in ROI 
and NI completed and awaiting data to come through. Consultants now working on optioneering the 
best fit route to be located within the Preferred Corridor in 2026 and environmental surveys will continue 
so as to aid in the draft of the EIAR. 
 
Carrick on Shannon to Battlebridge Blueway   
The consultants have to carry out further Aquatic surveys as per IFI Scoping response Opinion from An 
Coimisiún Pleanála submission. All other Environmental surveys are to be completed to keep surveys up 
to date for the Planning submission. PLO working with Landowners and Lisney Agronomists and 
Landowners Land valuers to get Voluntary land Acquisition agreement in place before submission to the 
Bord. They are also advancing the EIAR with a view that a Planning application will be lodged to An 
Coimisiún Pleanála at the end of November 2026, once a final Legal Review is complete 
  
South Leitrim Greenway  
TII formally approved Phase 0 and gave approval to move into Phase 1 Concept & Feasibility stage and to 
use TII Framework – Technical Consultancy Framework For Greenways and Active Travel Lot 1 (Ref: TII 
349) . TII gave approval for Phase 1 and Phase 2 which aligns with Cavan County Council TII approval for 
the Cavan Greenway project. Tender documents were uploaded to E-Tenders. Tenders have been 
submitted and are currently being assessed. 
  
Hartley Bridge 
Jons Civil Ltd was the successful tenderer for the Hartley Bridge Replacement Project and commenced 
works on site on 11 May 2026. Following a sequence of enabling works, including environmental 
management measures and local road diversion works, construction activities on the bridge abutments 
commenced. Good progress has been achieved to date, with works advancing particularly well on the 
Leitrim side of the River Shannon. Progress on the Roscommon side is slightly behind schedule but 
continues to move forward steadily. 
All in-stream works remain programmed for completion by the end of the Inland Fisheries Ireland 
approved in-stream works period. 
 
Dromod Roosky Greyway  
Stephen Reynolds Plant Hire has been appointed to complete the scheme and is expected to commence 
on site in the coming weeks. 
 
Acres Lake Facility Centre 
A substantial Completion Certificate has been issued for the Scheme and works are completed on site. 
We await the commissioning of the Access Control System for the building to become operational and 
open to the public. 
 
Narrow Gauge Trail Drumshanbo 
The trail is completed and open to the public. 
 
Fenagh Abbey Trail 
It is expected a planning application for a trail will be lodged in Aug 2026 subject to National Monuments 
agreement on scheme details.  
 
Carrick on Shannon Amenity Parks upgrade

15 
 
Part 8 Planning for the scheme is currently on public display. Application for funding to detail design and 
construct the scheme has been submitted to the Town and Cites Regeneration fund.  
Drumkeeran NW Stop Play and Therapy Centre 
Works are progressing steadily and remain on programme, with completion expected by mid-August 
2026. 
Ballinamore M.U.G.A. 
Following an eTenders competition, tenders are currently being assessed and it is intended to proceed 
with the appointment. Works are expected to commence in early August 2026, with completion 
anticipated during Q3 2026. 
Lurganboy Church of Ease 
Following two unsuccessful procurement competitions that attracted no submissions, quotations have 
been sought for a third time. The current submission deadline is 17 July 2026, after which it is hoped a 
contractor can be appointed. Works are expected to be completed during Q3 2026. 
Kinlough Men's Shed & Kayak Club 
Discussions are ongoing with the community groups regarding a potential shared PV system, as neither 
location is considered viable for a standalone system. Once agreement has been reached, a tender will 
be published for the supply and installation of a shared PV system serving both premises. 
Kinlough Arroo Project  
Tenders for the appointment of a Design Team for the Scheme and been assessed and it is expected that 
a Design Team will be appointed shortly.  
 
The Dock – Carrick on Shannon  
DHB Architects have been appointed as the Design Team for the scheme and design works has 
commenced with tender expected to be advertised in Q4 2026.

Activity under the Disabled Persons Grant Works on Local Authority Dwellings 
For 2026, Leitrim County Council submitted a funding request to the Department for DPG works to 31 
properties, consisting of adaptations to 30 no. properties and an extension to 1 no. property. Our 
funding request amounted to €284,670. In response, the Department provided Leitrim County Council 
with a funding allocation of €183,266 – a shortfall of €101,404 from what was requested. Therefore, 
Leitrim County Council have reduced our DPG programme for 2026 to now include adaptation works to 
30 no. properties.  
 
To date in 2026, works have been completed on DPG adaptations in 11 no. properties.

The Part 8 Public Consultation processes for 5 no. projects was completed / underway in June. A 
significant Active Travel project along the L-3412 Local Road in Carrick-on-Shannon along with junction 
improvement works in Drumshanbo were approved at their respective Municipal District meetings. Part 8 
processes are also underway for the refurbishment and change of use of the former courthouses in both 
Manorhamilton and Ballinamore and a proposed parks project for 4 areas in Carrick-on-Shannon. The 
latter 3 projects will be brought to the July meetings of their respective Municipal Districts.  
 
Forward Planning 
Variation to County Development Plan 2023-2029 
The proposed draft Variation to the County Development Plan 2023-2029 was published on 15th April with 
submissions invited by 13th May 2026. A total of 22 no. submissions were received from statutory bodies 
and individual landowners. The Chief Executive’s report in relation to the submissions received was 
published in early June and submitted to the Elected Members for their consideration. The matter will be 
considered further at the July Council meeting.  
Residential Zoned Land Tax (RZLT) 
Draft RZLT maps were published on Friday 30th January and public consultation ran until April 1st. 2 no. 
submissions were received requesting lands to be dezoned or rezoned. One of which relates to a site zoned 
residential use in Kinlough and the other of which is zoned residential in Drumshanbo. It is proposed to 
amend the zoning of both sites in the proposed variation to the County development Plan and the decision 
on each submission reflects same.   
Heritage   
• Leitrim County Council has received Shared Island grant funding as lead partner to carry out a joint 
cross boarded community project with Armagh City, Banbridge Craigavon Borough Council, which will 
celebrate the shared cultural heritage tradition of Mumming.  
• The Leitrim Community Holy Wells project is progressing. The archaeological field survey has been 
planned, and volunteer training took place in June.   
• The Leitrim Community Fieldnames project has commenced, with the project being promoted and 
volunteers being recruited to take part.  
• Two Connecting Through Heritage podcast episodes have been planned which will focus on the Leitrim 
Basket Project and the Leitrim Sweathouse Project.  
• Heritage Week 2026 events are being organised for August.  
• The Community Monument Fund 2026 projects continue to be managed for both the Old Church of 
Ireland, Manorhamilton conservation works and the Manorhamilton Castle Conservation Management 
Plan.  
• The Leitrim Heritage Plan 2026 – 2031 is progressing with the final layout design having being 
commissioned.
